title: Missouri Airman provides relief after Hurricane Harvey
description: U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Kyle Twenter, a pilot assigned to the 180th Airlift Squadron, Missouri Air National Guard, talks about his experience assisting relief efforts in Texas after Hurricane Harvey from Aug. 29 to Sept. 1, 2017.
keywords: Missouri National Guard, 139th Airlift Wing, disaster relief, Hurricane Harvey, Texas
credit: Tech. Sgt. Theodore Ramsey, Theodore Ramsey

transcript.text: (gentle guitar music)
- [Kyle] Harvey made landfall on Friday night,
^down in the Port Aransas,
^Port Lavaca area, north of Corpus Christi,
and we had two crews that went out
immediately that first weekend.
They notified us at noon last week
that we were gonna reposition to Texas
to be closer to the center of all the disaster
and be attached to the Air Operations Center in Texas
that was running all the air mobility for the Harvey relief.
So we had an idea that we would be doing security forces,
taking security forces into the area,
taking in cargo, water, food,
supplies, blankets, cots.
You have an idea of what you're doing
and it turns out that's what we were doing,
taking supplies in, taking evacuees out,
and then repositioning other guardsmen around the region,
so they could be where they need to be.
You know, we went into there, we were one of
the first airplanes to go into Beaumont, and
we had no idea really what to expect.
I mean, we know we're doing evacuation operations,
but you don't really know until
you get there and you start doing it.
We had everything from infants to the elderly,
we had wheelchairs, we had pets.
There were some people who had never been
on an airplane before, and this was their first
flying experience of their life.
Can you imagine?
Being evacuated out of your home, out of your city.
You've never gotten out much and now
you're on your first airplane ride ever.
Some people didn't even know where they were going:
they were asking us, "where are we going?"
and we're telling them,
"Oh, we're taking you to Dallas, Texas".
Some of the folks were very nervous about flying
because they hadn't flown before.
We had candy that we handed out
to make it a little bit more enjoyable for them.
We had a bag full of teddy bears for the kids.
This is what we do in the Guard,
and we all love our jobs, Monday through Friday:
but when you're now getting called on to do
the real mission of the Guard,
which is to be citizen soldiers
and to take care of our own country
and our own people in a time of devastation,
it's very rewarding.
